recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Turkey Cutlets with Fresh Tomato-Basil Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick pan-seared turkey cutlet, cooked to a golden-brown crust, is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The whole turkey piece is generously topped with a vibrant fresh tomato-basil salsa. The salsa showcases small, bright red tomato cubes, contrasting with vibrant green basil leaves and tiny specks of minced garlic. A cluster of tender-crisp roasted asparagus spears, retaining their bright green color, is neatly arranged alongside the turkey. A fresh lemon wedge rests near the cutlet. The plate is set on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned nearby. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh textures and appealing colors. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere, subtly blurred to focus on the food. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Pat turkey cutlets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Mince garlic. Coarsely chop basil. In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, minced garlic, chopped basil, 15ml olive oil, and balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Set aside.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, or until tender-crisp.
Heat a large non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat with remaining 15ml olive oil. Place turkey cutlets in hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Place one turkey cutlet on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of tomato-basil salsa over the turkey. Arrange roasted asparagus alongside. Serve immediately with a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure turkey reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
